findings.F1: The tested day measure points the wrong way at the next day and is not graded at ten days. Pooled over every profile on its 1-day grid, a day's move in 30-day swing units predicts the next day's unusual move with a Spearman rho of -0.10 (p 1e-15, 6261 cases). After days of -2 swings or worse the next day is +1.92 % (t 3.25, 131 cases), and after days of 0 to +1 swings it is -0.32 % (t -2.89, 2015 cases). Inside choppy calm the 10-day cases are too few to grade (7 cases at +1 to +2 swings, 4 above +2). This next-day rebound after falls is the long rebound the map already holds in many cells.
findings.F2: In calm markets a coin's 5-day return keeps going the same way over the next 10 days, and more so the larger it was in swing units. The continuation is -1.41 % for 0 to 1 swings, +0.85 % for 1 to 2, +1.93 % for 2 to 3 and +7.95 % above 3 (t 2.48, 47 cases on 23 days). Calm here is a 30-day swing below the coin's pooled median, an approximation of the profile's past-year percentile.
findings.F3: In agitated markets the same 5-day measure is not graded. It gives +2.53 % for 0 to 1 swings, -4.93 % for 1 to 2 (t -2.04), +0.24 % for 2 to 3 and +6.65 % above 3 (t 2.28, 27 days). This is consistent with continuation being an orderly-market effect.

findings.F5: Pooled 5-day falls of 3 swings or more are followed by -13.6 % over 10 days (t -6.06 ordinary; -2.28 and -3.46 day-clustered in the two deepest bins). The result is negative on all six coins, but it sits on only 11 days in windows w7, w14 and w16. It is a few crash episodes, not a broad pattern.

ideas.idea: In a calm market, the larger a coin's 5-day return against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the further it keeps moving the same way over the next 10 days, falls continuing down as rises continue up.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a quiet market follows a strong 5-day move in its own direction for ten days, including shorting sharp quiet-market declines rather than buying them.
ideas.name: calm multi-day move continues
